role: Promulgating agency for Average Fuel Economy Standard
stance_basis: agency promulgates and defends the 17.2 mpg fuel economy standard as appropriate and representing maximum feasible average fuel economy
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is the promulgating agency for the Average Fuel Economy Standard for Nonpassenger Automobiles for Model Year 1979, concluding that 17.2 mpg is the appropriate standard and that a separate 15.8 mpg standard should apply to four-wheel drive recreational vehicles. NHTSA prepared the Final Environmental Impact Statement, analyzing a range of possible standards (16.4–18.7 mpg) and their environmental impacts, and determined the standard represents the maximum feasible average fuel economy for MY 1979. The agency supports the action as beneficial due to significant gasoline savings and relatively minor adverse environmental impacts.
complaint_summary: NHTSA acknowledges uncertainty in attributing fuel economy improvements to the AFES versus voluntary manufacturer plans, and notes that MY 1979 test procedures may produce lower reported fuel economy, meaning actual savings could exceed EIS estimates.

statement.text:
The agency recognizes that there is some merit to each of these positions on the relationship between the AFES program and the measures to improve average fuel economy that will be taken up to MY 1979. The correct viewpoint is probably at some indeterminate point between these extremes.
Fuel economy test procedures for MY 1979 are different from those in effect for MY 1976. A vehicle tested to both procedures would likely show a lower reported fuel economy for the MY 1979 test procedures. Fuel savings described in this EIS were determined based on a comparison of fuel economies for the MY 1976 procedures. If the MY 1979 procedures produce results closer to real-world experience and result in lower reported fuel economy, all other things being equal, the actual savings would be more than described in the EIS.

summary_quote: The agency has concluded that the appropriate fuel economy standard for non-passenger automobiles in model year 1979 should be 17.2 mpg.
